title: Introducing ChatGPT Wallet
summary: OpenAI announcement (13 Nov 2026). ChatGPT Wallet lets agents in ChatGPT Work, Codex and dots complete purchases with user approval. OpenAI describes it as the first wallet where agents pay without access to the user's actual card details and with a security check for every purchase, preserving card rewards and dispute protections. Built with American Express, Mastercard and Visa. Initially rolling out in dots to ChatGPT Pro subscribers aged 18+ in the US with eligible US-issued cards. Websites must ensure agents are not inadvertently blocked; payment and risk systems must recognise legitimate agent purchases.

title: ChatGPT's new Wallet lets AI agents shop and check out for you
summary: TechCrunch (13 Nov 2026): OpenAI launched a wallet that lets its agents (dots) help choose and complete purchases. Limited rollout to US ChatGPT Pro subscribers 18+ with US-issued Visa, Mastercard or American Express. Users review items, total and card before checkout and approve with a security check such as Face ID or fingerprint, which creates a transaction record. Some retailers block AI agents; the report names Amazon as the largest retailer to ban them. OpenAI also published a Commerce Partner Playbook for merchants supporting agents.

title: Supporting research on AI and children's safety
summary: OpenAI commits $2 million to research on AI and children's safety, supporting shared tools to measure risks.

title: Tokayev Calls for Stronger Logistics and Digitalization at Security Council Meeting
summary: At an operational Security Council meeting on 13 Nov 2026, President Tokayev called for efficiency and modernisation of transport and logistics: more logistics centres, simpler border and customs procedures, removing infrastructure bottlenecks. He criticised national railway operator Kazakhstan Temir Zholy (KTZ), urging better profitability and operational efficiency, including through digitalisation. He addressed the detention of senior Samruk-Kazyna and KTZ executives on suspicion of corruption-related offences and stressed personal accountability and transparency. Agencies were instructed to strengthen international transport corridors through Kazakhstan; the Security Council Secretariat oversees implementation. No figures or deadlines given.

title: Kazakhstan, Austria Seek to Expand Trade and Investment Cooperation
summary: Kazakh and Austrian officials discussed deeper trade and investment ties in transport, energy, petrochemicals and critical raw materials, ahead of an intergovernmental commission meeting in Vienna.

title: Kazakhstan Advances Nuclear Power Plans, Considers Sites for Third Facility
summary: Agency for Atomic Energy chairman Almasadam Satkaliyev, speaking at World Atomic Week in Antalya on 13 Nov 2026: Rosatom with Kazakh partners could begin building the first plant in 2027 if Kazakh legal requirements are met; technical annexes to the EPC contract are still being negotiated. Second plant: negotiations and surveys ongoing, too early for timelines. First and second plants preliminarily planned in Zhambyl District, Almaty Region. Third-plant candidate sites: Kurchatov (East Kazakhstan), the Caspian coast, and northern regions along the Tobol River (recommended by grid operator KEGOC); choice depends on regional demand, geology, hydrology and cooling water. No capacity figures given. Kazakhstan holds a Framatome licence to make fuel for French-designed reactors; plans a multi-level strategic uranium reserve for at least 100 years of domestic supply. Kazakhstan ranks second in uranium reserves and produces about 40% of world output.

title: Kazakhstan, Uzbekistan Sign Memorandum to Protect and Restore Saiga Population
summary: Kazakhstan and Uzbekistan signed an agreement on 12 Nov to conserve saigas by protecting migration routes, restoring habitats, monitoring populations and fighting poaching.

title: From Paper to Digital: Kazakhstan's Tenge Marks 33 Years
summary: Kazakhstan marks the 33rd anniversary of the tenge, tracing its evolution from the first banknotes to the digital tenge, which launched in July.

title: Archaeologists Discover Turkic Khaganate-Era Settlement in East Kazakhstan
summary: A KazNU expedition found the Kalzhyr settlement (over 25 hectares) in the Zaysan Basin, East Kazakhstan, between the villages of Kalzhyr and Boran. Finds and radiocarbon analysis date it to the 6th–7th centuries AD; early findings suggest construction during the First Turkic Khaganate. Finds: fire-damaged fortifications, interior structures with ornamented plaster, charred wheat and legume grains, ceramics including a rare bird figurine with a rattle, and a Late Bronze Age kereksur burial structure. Expedition leader Nikita Konstantinov says the kereksur extends knowledge of the western boundary of such monuments, mainly found in Xinjiang and Mongolia. Methods included aerial and thermal imaging; data will feed digital models and a regional GIS. Findings described as preliminary; no peer-reviewed publication mentioned.

title: Kazakh Filmmakers of Independence Offer No Answers: This May Be Their Greatest Strength
summary: Film scholar Gulnara Abikeeva examines the 'Children of Independence' generation of Kazakh filmmakers, whose critical, non-ideological work has earned international festival attention.

title: Kazakhstan Apple Fruit Industry Observes Challenges as Global Market Shifts
summary: Kazakhstan is expanding state support for orchards as global apple exports fall. The country produced 205,200 tonnes in 2025 but still relies heavily on imports.

title: Analysis: Climate-finance pledges fall 70% as countries meet at COP31
summary: Carbon Brief analysis: public climate finance pledged to developing countries has fallen by more than 70%. Previous pledges were about $42bn a year; current pledges average about $11.7bn a year over the rest of the 2020s (article mixes £ and $; check basis). Only five nations announced new multi-year pledges (NRDC/E3G tracker); the UK is the only major donor among them, averaging about $5.7bn a year — roughly half of all pledged annual funds. European Commission about $4.5bn a year to 2027; Canada CA$5.3bn by 2030 (~$860m/yr). Germany, France and Japan have no new multi-year pledges; the US provides no official climate finance; co-host Australia also absent. Covers 23 developed countries plus the EU. Causes cited by experts: conflict, fiscal constraints, defence spending, US Paris withdrawal, political shifts in Europe. Caveats: pledges are not spending; official 2025 data not yet available.

title: COP31: How Ed Miliband answered Carbon Brief readers' questions
summary: UK foreign secretary Ed Miliband answered Carbon Brief readers' questions at COP31 in Antalya, Turkey.

title: Analysis: Which countries have sent the most delegates to COP31?
summary: More than 92,000 people registered to attend COP31 in Antalya, Turkey, potentially among the largest COPs.

title: A Global Rebound for Mangroves
summary: NASA Earth Observatory (13 Nov 2026) on Zhang et al. (2026), Science vol. 392: Landsat imagery 1984–2023 — described as the first long-term global mangrove maps. 1984–2010: losses of nearly 3,000 km²; after 2010: gains of nearly 2,000 km², with denser canopies in many forests, especially South America. About two-thirds of expansion is colonisation of new areas, one-third restoration and regrowth. Gains led by Asia, Australia and South America; Burma lost ~28.6% of mangrove area from the 1980s to 2010, then grew ~10%. Losses continue in the Niger Delta; cyclone damage in North America and southern Africa. Causes: sediment creating mudflats, warming at range edges, restoration and legal protection. Lead author Zhen Zhang (Tulane) warns gains are no grounds for complacency. Mangroves store up to four times as much carbon as taller inland tropical forests.

title: Outbursts from a Massive Star
summary: AT 2016blu, a star at least 33 solar masses in galaxy NGC 4559, about 30 million light-years away, has brightened and dimmed regularly for over 15 years, with outbursts every 113 days. Chandra X-ray data suggest a hidden companion — a stellar-mass black hole or a neutron star — pulls material from the star as they orbit; the material heats and emits X-rays. Companion inferred, not directly seen. Credits M. Aghakhanloo et al. (University of Virginia); no journal named on the page.

title: Gemini Astronaut Photos Inspired Early Earth Observation Program
summary: Orbital photos from Gemini XII and other Gemini flights showed the value of space imagery for studying Earth, helping justify the satellite programme that led to Landsat.

title: Fugitive imagination
summary: Essay by Shahram Khosravi arguing that people who are confined, displaced or silenced develop hidden forms of knowledge and imagination.

title: Why anything exists
summary: Essay by Andrew T Brenner offering a new response to why there is something rather than nothing.
